summary: All three orders filled as decided: BND sold in full at $70.62, MCO bought for $25 at $509.04, and VTI bought for $15 (half the proposed $25) at $368.94. Equity closed at $626.32 (day -$2.46, drawdown 1.55%) while SPY's mark fell about 1.9% to 739.95. The account is still ahead of both benchmarks: +4.39% against the shadow's +3.51% and SPY's -3.46%, and since v6 started on 11-10 it is +0.61% against -1.07% and -1.33%. The decision holds up on its reasoning. The BND exit followed the position's own stored sell condition and the Market Analyst's L8 point that duration is not hedging, and it was tax-clean. MCO fills a favored sector and is sized for the MSCI overlap (L3). The weakest call was VTI. The Skeptic's timing case was strong: Nvidia reports 11-17, the Proposer had already said a one-day delay costs little, and VTI adds the same cap-weighted exposure the Market Analyst called the riskiest part of the tape. I split the difference with a half-size buy, when the cleaner answer was to defer it one session. The cost is small (the new lot is about -1.2%), and today's drop isn't the reason to say so. The reason is that I argued for waiting and then bought anyway. The bigger risk now is structural. VOO and VTI (about 23.5% of equity) share one stop, SPY's 200-day at 729.31, and both are NEAR at +1.46% going into the Nvidia print. One SPY close below that level trips almost a quarter of the book at once. Cash is still about 13.7%. The deployment commitment after the 11-17 and 11-19 prints stands, but it should go to favored-sector single names and not to more SPY-stopped beta. Two L6 gaps from today need fixing: MCO's stored invalidation text says 'more than 8% below avg_entry_price', but the stored stop is $470, which is 7.7% under the $509.04 fill, so the text and the number disagree. VTI's text likewise names avg_entry_price instead of a dollar level. Its blended cost is now about $375.2, so the 8% clause is about $345.20.
lessons: When the Proposer concedes that a one-day delay costs little and a dated binary event (here Nvidia's 11-17 print) lands the next session, defer the buy instead of half-sizing it. Half-sizing kept the risk I had argued against and dropped only part of it.

Count how much equity shares one stop before adding to it. VOO and VTI both stop on SPY's 200-day, so adding VTI raised the share of the book that one SPY close can trip (now about 23.5%, NEAR at +1.46%). New deployment should go to names with their own stops.

When a buy fills, restate its stop text as a dollar level from the actual fill in the next run's thesis_updates (L6). Today MCO's text ('more than 8% below avg_entry_price') contradicts its $470 stop_price (7.7% under the $509.04 fill), and VTI's text has no dollar level (about $345.20 from the $375.2 blended cost). Tomorrow's decision should fix both.

WMT's 8-K 5.02 filed 11-16 is still unread with the 11-19 print two sessions away. If the filing turns out to be a senior executive departure, the next run should bring the WMT reduction I asked for, not let it carry into the print.
